rawOutput.title: Personal Finance Fundamentals
rawOutput.topic: Budgeting, credit, debt, and index-fund investing
rawOutput.rationale: This is a mixed conceptual and problem-solving plan. It begins with practical cash-flow decisions, then builds the interest and credit foundation needed to evaluate debt and investing. The final session retrieves and applies the full sequence. Sessions fit the three available weekly windows and use focused, task-led examples with support adjusted from each attempt.

sessions.title: Build a Working Budget
sessions.objective: Turn income, expenses, and savings priorities into a usable monthly budget.
sessions.amountLabel: One monthly cash-flow model and one adjustment decision
contentTargets: A simple monthly budget with a savings buffer
completionEvidence: Classify sample expenses as fixed, variable, or irregular
Construct a balanced monthly budget from a sample income
Explain one adjustment needed when expenses exceed income

sessions.title: Understand Credit and Interest
sessions.objective: Explain how borrowing costs grow and how common actions affect credit.
sessions.amountLabel: One interest comparison and one credit-use scenario
contentTargets: Principal, interest rate, APR, and compounding
Payment history, credit utilization, and responsible credit use
completionEvidence: Explain how APR and compounding affect borrowing cost
Compare the cost of two borrowing offers
Apply credit-use principles to a sample credit-card scenario

sessions.title: Prioritize and Manage Debt
sessions.objective: Create a practical repayment order while maintaining essential cash reserves.
sessions.amountLabel: One debt inventory and one repayment plan
contentTargets: Debt balances, rates, minimum payments, and total cost
completionEvidence: Classify sample debts by urgency and borrowing cost
Compare two repayment approaches for a sample debt list
Construct a repayment order with a brief justification

sessions.title: Index Funds and an Integrated Money Plan
sessions.objective: Explain index-fund basics and apply budgeting, debt, and investing principles to one financial plan.
sessions.amountLabel: One index-fund evaluation and one integrated financial plan
contentTargets: Diversification, index funds, fees, risk, and time horizon
The relationship among emergency savings, expensive debt, and long-term investing
completionEvidence: Explain how an index fund differs from an individual stock
Compare two sample index funds using diversification and fees
Construct a prioritized plan covering budgeting, debt repayment, emergency savings, and investing
